newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean bank shrs down on SEOULBANK, weak market.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean bank shrs down on SEOULBANK, weak market.

text.p: South Korean bank shares slid in Monday morning trading as the weekend arrest of the head of a leading South Korean bank pressured already weak counters, analysts said.
The banking sub-index was down 0.59 percent to 427.78 at 10:42 a.m. (0142 GMT).

On Saturday, state prosecutors said they had arrested Sohn Hong-gyun, president of SEOULBANK, on bribery charges. SEOULBANK is South Korea's sixth largest bank in terms of deposits, and its shares fell 100 won to 4,500 won in active trading.

"The SEOULBANK scandal is hurting bank shares, but the biggest reason for the fall is that financial shares are falling in line with the market's doldrums," said Lee Sang-koo, a Hyundai Securities market analyst.
One reason the sector was not falling further was that the scandal was seen as potentially helpful in the long-term in speeding up banking industry reforms.
"This could set up motion for structural changes in the banking industry," said Shinyoung Securities market analyst Steven Lee.
He recommended bank stocks as a "trading buy" if the share prices fell any further.
Korea First Bank shares fell 20 won to 4,980 and Korea Exchange Bank was unchanged at 7,700.
